title: Thiol reactivity and ferroptosis sensitization as toxic mechanisms of the phthalimide pesticides folpet and captan
content:
Abstract
Captan and folpet are phthalimide fungicides widely used in agricultural and nonagricultural settings and have been identified as environmental risk factors for Parkinson’s disease (PD). These pesticides are highly reactive with cellular thiols, particularly glutathione (GSH), disrupting redox homeostasis and inducing neuronal toxicity; however, the mechanisms underlying their neurotoxicity remain poorly understood. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death characterized by impaired antioxidant defenses, including GSH depletion and phospholipid peroxidation. This study examined whether captan and folpet induce or modulate ferroptosis in immortalized neuronal and non-neuronal cell lines. Cytotoxicity and intracellular GSH levels were assessed using calcein AM and monochlorobimane assays, respectively. Captan and folpet showed marked cytotoxicity in mouse hippocampal neurons (HT-22), with IC50 values of ∼5 and ∼10 μM, respectively. Co-treatment with the thiol-containing compounds N-acetylcysteine and dithiothreitol markedly protected against toxicity induced by both pesticides, supporting thiol reactivity as an important mechanism underlying their toxicity. In addition, captan and folpet did not substantially induce ferroptotic cell death on their own; they significantly enhanced susceptibility to RSL3-induced ferroptotic stress while attenuating erastin-induced cytotoxicity. These differential effects may reflect the distinct mechanisms by which RSL3 and erastin initiate ferroptotic stress, together with the thiol-reactive properties of captan and folpet. Collectively, these findings identify context-dependent modulation of ferroptotic susceptibility as a previously unrecognized mechanism that may contribute to the cellular effects of these PD-associated pesticides.
